fact: The article says Tunisia's entrepreneurial ecosystem is carried by a pioneering Startup Act.
The article describes the Startup Act as the legal framework promoting startups in Tunisia, on which the JICA programme draws.
The column cites 1,450 labelled startups in Tunisia.
Minister Sofiane Hmissi said a revised bill, Startup Act 2.0, is in preparation with the Ministry of Economy and Planning, keeping the earlier legal framework.
Agence Ecofin reports that about 1,400 enterprises hold the 'Start-up' label in 2026, with the government aiming for 2,000 in 2027.

The digital ministry's guide sets out Law No. 2018-20 of 17 April 2018 on startups and Government Decree No. 2018-840 of 11 October 2018 on the Startup label, with corporate tax exemption, a startup grant, a guarantee fund for startups and tax deductions for startup investors.

The CDC director-general said in a July interview that the CDC had financed 10 investment funds under ANAVA, with 70 Tunisian startups benefiting from financing through the fund of funds and its funds.
Minister Sofiene Hemissi said on 17 April 2026 that his ministry is working with several ministries on a Startup Act 2.0 bill.
Startup Tunisia's results page lists the June 2026 labelling session as granting 7 labels and 9 pre-labels from 40 applications.

ANAVA, Tunisia's fund of funds backed by the World Bank, CDC and KfW and run by Smart Capital under the government's Startup Tunisia programme, committed USD 4 million to the Rasmal Innovation Fund, a venture fund investing in startups.
El Ghazala Technopark's Monia Jendoubi told national radio that 1214 startups held the startup label up to July 2025, with 8-year tax exemption, grant eligibility and a foreign-currency account.
L'Economiste Maghrebin quotes the head of Smart Tunisian Technoparks saying Tunisia has the Startup Act, in application for six years, and that ministries are working on an amendment.
The World Bank blog says national policies like the Startup Act have paved the way for a thriving community of entrepreneurs.
Smart Tunisian Technoparks CEO Rim Saied says 1,133 companies held the startup label by end October 2024.
